title: One skill per lesson
statement: Teach at most one well-defined new skill or named procedure per lesson, remove anything that doesn't serve it, and let its review steps use only skills already taught.
detail: A pedagogy framework's first attribute of a good lesson is a single objective, and its path to mastery focuses each lesson 'on a single, well-defined skill' (`icloud-work/incept/incept-uae-api-website/bench.inceptapi.com/Incept Pedagogy & Learning Science Overview.md`). Its cognitive-load rule removes the rest: lessons 'eliminate unnecessary complexity, visuals, and multitasking'. It is an adopted rule, with no measurement in the project.
against: The project's own page on direct instruction records a criticism of the approach: '- May not fully encourage critical thinking or open-ended exploration' (`icloud-work/incept/incept-uae-api-website/bench.inceptapi.com/content/english/pages/direct-instruction.md`, line 63). Review across units is unsettled: the lint's lesson contract records cross-unit review identity as an open question (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/handoffs/g3-reading-v2-feedback-2026-07-16/tooling/ti-courseplans-2169d1f/scripts/lane-tools/op-lint/lesson-schema.md`, lines 73-74).

evidence.quote: Each lesson targets one skill or concept only. Students should know exactly what they are learning and why it matters.
Each focuses on a single, well-defined skill.
Lessons eliminate unnecessary complexity, visuals, and multitasking. Students focus on one process at a time.
4. **Design for cognitive load limits.** Keep granularity tight, reduce noise, avoid bundling multiple new skills in one lesson.
| L6 | one new operation per dose | every non-review atom carries exactly the lesson's one `operation_id`. Catches the round-2 skill-switching you-do (together with L1). |
(an undeclared new operation cannot be smuggled in as phase:"review").
Spec is silent on cross-unit review identity - recorded as an open question.

evidence.path: 5. Curriculum/Instruction/3.2 - The Living World - Lesson Designs/3.2 - The Living World - Complete KB.xlsx
evidence.quote: FIND fits the fact-based texts (Plants, Mammals, Invertebrates, Microorganisms). The comparison texts (Feathers and Scales, Life in Water) use CONNECT - compare two groups, then draw the deeper link. The Animal Kingdom uses SORT (classify by shared features); the persuasion texts (Rainforests, Whose World Is It) need WEIGH / fact-vs-opinion.
